angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 673,438 km at 84.58 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 11.8236 +/- 0.0108 mas (same row, RUWE 0.96): 84.58 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.968 +/- 0.036 solar radii from Dai et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1136 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165...33D/abstract): 673,438 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.022 +/- 0.027 solar masses from Dai et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1136 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165...33D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5770 +/- 50 K from Dai et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1136 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165...33D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Dai et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1136 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165...33D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1136.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.476, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
